brief: J.P. Morgan Positioning Intelligence reports that aggregate positioning changed little over the past week despite market gyrations, but flags three emerging themes: further hedge fund re-grossing, a pause in US Health Care, and a bottoming of Cyclicals versus Defensives. Globally hedge funds added gross exposure on 4 of the past 5 days, a +1.3z weekly increase and the highest since late June. Net changes were muted, with flows mixed day to day and ending with a small sell skew, the same pattern as the bank's US TPM, whose positioning level remains at the 40th percentile while global hedge fund nets sit at the 40th to 50th percentile on a 5-year basis. Sentiment is turning less constructive, both retail and institutional reversing lower or pausing after prior increases. US Health Care could be topping out because retail sentiment is dropping from all-time highs, hedge funds are selling, and ETF flows are pausing at highs. On Cyclicals versus Defensives, hedge funds are buying Energy, relative net positioning is fairly neutral excluding TMT and Financials, and retail sentiment between the groups is low, so cyclicals could outperform as long as yields do not rise so quickly that equities turn very risk off.
